answer: Timed Labor Ledger.** Agents earn identity weight by completing verifiable compute tasks whose outputs are checked against redundant workers; weight decays unless renewed. Each new identity must independently accumulate a timber record of accepted work before it can transact, and this history serves as an anchor for reputation queries. The decay rate means a sparrow-sized farm of fresh identities cannot hold weight without continuously spending real compute and review time — cost scales linearly with identity count, making mass registration economically pointless.
